findings.claim: No installer step or compose overlay raises the orchestrator's 4 GiB cap (TB_MEM_ORCH), not even the reference workstation's; SCREEN of the whole hospital needs 4.37 GiB at 50,000 patients and 8.22 GiB at 100,000, so it is killed there as shipped
findings.expected: the orchestrator's cap sized for the hospital the box screens, or SCREEN bounded in memory
findings.happened: 4 GiB on every shape; SCREEN finished only with TB_MEM_ORCH=10g

findings.claim: The cascade's S1 keeps every patient's rows at every index date as Python dictionaries (_s1_rows, to_pylist of each batch): 2.08 GiB traced in 12.6 million allocations at 50,000 patients, S1's resident peak 5.31 GiB at 100,000, where the gate's cascade is killed at the 4 GiB cap
findings.expected: S1's memory bounded like the lake's batches (D-748)
findings.happened: the rows of all batches held at once, then indexed again by patient

findings.claim: The cascade's S1 time grows with about the square of the patients (243 s at 50,000, 902 s at 100,000 for one study; 807 s of it reading the rows in D-748's batches), the pattern H-23 showed for FEAS
findings.expected: S1 time near linear in the patients
findings.happened: 3.7 times the time for twice the patients

findings.claim: The scale gate's ingest runs the HL7 validator only when TB_HL7_VALIDATOR_JAR and the packages are set, and its report does not say which check ran; one size's ingest differs about 2 times between the two (20,000: 241 s with it, 110 s without)
findings.expected: the report names the validator that ran
findings.happened: the same command gave 177 s and 328 s at 20,000 in H-23 with no record of why
